current: Both events fire and both carry the documented `trigger`, but neither carries its second documented field. packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:149-154 types the Pi event as `{ reason?: string }` and emits `{ hook_event_name: 'PreCompact', trigger: compactTrigger(event?.reason), source }`; :155-161 does the same for `PostCompact`. `compactTrigger` (:81-83) is correct — manual stays manual, threshold/overflow/absent map to auto, proven by lifecycle-bridge.test.ts:198-228. The values exist one property access away and are dropped: Pi passes `customInstructions` into `session_before_compact` on the manual path (node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/agent-session.js:1316-1324, typed `SessionBeforeCompactEvent.customInstructions?: string` at dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:430-441) and `undefined` on the auto path (agent-session.js:1544-1553) — which is exactly Claude's "For `auto`, `custom_instructions` is empty"; and it passes the saved `compactionEntry` into `session_compact` (agent-session.js:1362-1369, :1605-1612) whose `CompactionEntry.summary: string` is at @earendil-works/pi-agent-core/dist/harness/types.d.ts:253-259. Nessy's own manual path already carries the instructions end to end: pi-agent.ts:6068 `requestCompact(customInstructions)` -> packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:3909 `handle.compact(msg.customInstructions)`. The frozen contract rows that document the payload also list only the two fields: packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:83-84 `redactedPayload: ['trigger', 'source']`. `SdkAutomationInput` (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742-768) declares `trigger` and `source` but has no `custom_instructions` / `compact_summary` member. packages/shared/src/automations/sdk-bridge.ts:62 states, now falsely by omission, "SessionEnd, Stop, PreCompact, PermissionRequest, Setup have no additional fields". Nothing downstream strips fields — packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-650 `hookCommandStdinPayload` spreads `{...input}` onto hook stdin verbatim and :53 puts the same JSON in `NESSY_EVENT_DATA` — so the loss is entirely at the emitter. `grep -a` over the repo finds zero producers of either snake_case name outside `docs/`.
divergence: Two documented input fields are absent from the emitted payload; everything else about the two events (names, matcher `trigger`, once-per-occurrence delivery, observational kind) already matches. This is an omission, not a misnaming: there is no wrongly-keyed value to rename, and the extra Nessy-only `source` (Pi's raw `manual|threshold|overflow`) is additive and not contradicted by the page. Consequence: a documented `PostCompact` hook that reads `.compact_summary` gets `undefined`, and a `PreCompact` hook that reads `.custom_instructions` after `/compact <text>` gets `undefined` rather than the user's text (Claude would give `""` on the auto path and the text on the manual path).

blastRadius: Crosses the subprocess->host IPC wire: the payload is sent as `{ type: 'automation_event', event, input }` from packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1969 and :2958 (typed `OutboundAutomationEvent` at :498) and consumed at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:2340-2343 with a bare `as SdkAutomationInput` cast — no runtime schema validation, so two optional string fields are additive and backward-compatible in both directions, but this IS a wire boundary and therefore a repo risk trigger. It also crosses the hook trust boundary: the input object reaches user code verbatim through `hookCommandStdinPayload` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-650) on stdin and through `NESSY_EVENT_DATA` (:53) in the environment, for BOTH execution authorities — the direct spawn at hook-command.ts:737 and the host's sandboxed runner at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4488 — and it is handed unchanged to prompt/agent/mcp plugin hook runners (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1436-1441). Privacy note worth stating in the commit: `compact_summary` is conversation content that has never previously left the app into a hook process; hook-command.ts:634-639 records the deliberate decision that stdin is unredacted and redaction lives on the output path, so this is consistent, but a user-configured webhook action on `PostCompact` would now ship a conversation summary off-machine. No persistence boundary: agent events do not go through the event bus (packages/shared/src/automations/automation-system.ts:651-653), so `events.jsonl` is unaffected. Tests that must move: packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.test.ts:47-56 (exact `toEqual`, will fail) and :198-228. Matching is untouched — `getMatchValueForSdkInput` reads `trigger` only (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:203-205), covered by packages/shared/src/automations/conditions.test.ts:627-630. The second, unreachable executor in packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts (dead per packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.test.ts:6) needs no change. The Claude and Codex backends never emit these two events, so imported-plugin hooks only see them on Pi sessions.
userImpact: A user who writes the page's own PostCompact recipe — "log the generated summary or update external state" — gets nothing. Concretely: add a command action on `PostCompact` in Settings -> Automations (or install a Claude plugin whose hooks.json targets it), run a session until auto-compaction, and the hook's stdin is `{"hook_event_name":"PostCompact","trigger":"auto","source":"threshold"}` — `jq -r .compact_summary` prints `null`, so the log line or the external state update is empty. Symmetrically, run `/compact Focus on the API surface`: the PreCompact hook sees `trigger: "manual"` but no `custom_instructions`, so a hook that mirrors the user's compaction intent into an external system cannot. Compaction itself is correct and the summary is used normally — only the hook payload is short, so nothing is visible unless a hook is installed on these two events.
